criterion: signature/rename whose call sites are not all updated
finding: seed_map --config PATH still runs raw parse then validate, so the CHILD_KEYS change makes it refuse a file that holds jira.credentials-env.
why: The removed key is dropped only by the owner filter; this caller skips it, so a file afk-config.py validate accepts with a warning now makes seed_map exit 2, against AC-027 'a set value is ignored'.
fix: Make the reader's validate accept a removed key (it is warned and dropped elsewhere), or drop REMOVED_KEYS before validate; pin it with a test.
evidence: seed_map.py:295 `config = module.deep_merge(dict(module.DEFAULTS), module.parse(text, str(path)))` then :296 `problems = module.validate(config, repo)`; callers.md PROBE-7 `ConfigError jira.credentials-env: unknown key`

criterion: Acceptance: no fallback code reads an ignored value (ADR-0001, ADR-0007)
finding: The no-Python fallback still greps every raw file for repo-hooks, including files the owner rule ignores for that team setting.
why: repo-hooks is a team setting; the reader ignores it in the machine file and, with a committed file, in the personal file and local overlay, but this fallback still blocks the commit on a value there.
fix: Limit the fallback's layers to the files a team setting is read from: the committed file, else the personal file and local overlay, plus $AFK_CONFIG.
evidence: precommit-gates.sh:192-195 `for layer in "${AFK_CONFIG:-}" .afk/config.local.yaml "$common/afk/config.yaml" .afk/config.yaml "${HOME:-/nonexistent}/.afk/config.yaml"`; ADR-0007 "No fallback code reads them."

criterion: Acceptance: jira.credentials-env is removed from the schema
finding: The init scaffold still suggests the removed jira.credentials-env and writes notes and the forge remote into the committed file, where both are ignored.
why: A fresh init followed by validate prints ignored-value warnings on a file init itself wrote.
fix: Drop the credentials-env lines (offer a commented site line), and stop writing notes and the forge remote block into the committed scaffold.
evidence: afk-config.py:1192 `"#   credentials-env:          # variable NAMES; never a secret",`; :1162 `"notes: repo-files",`; :1213 `lines += [f"{forge}:", f"  remote: {remote or 'origin'}", ""]`

criterion: Acceptance: a machine setting in any repository file is ignored (AC-023, ADR-0007)
finding: The notion kind's instructions still read the machine-owned notion.parent-page-id directly from the committed .afk/config.yaml.
why: The owner rule ignores that value in every repository file, but the agent-run path reads it raw.
fix: Have NOTES.md read the value through `afk-config.py get notion.parent-page-id`.

criterion: caller whose contract changed not updated
finding: The obsidian kind no longer roots at the vault, but its documents still say so and both kinds' notes_root functions are now orphans; D-11's 'later slice' is named by no contract.
why: No subtask Scope lists adapters/notes/obsidian/*, adapters/notes/repo-files/notes.sh, ADAPTERS.md or providers/CONFORMANCE.md.
fix: Update the stale documents and remove the dead notes_root functions, or anchor the work to a named subtask.
evidence: CONFORMANCE.md:93 'the vault directory removed → {"unavailable": true} exit 4'; obsidian/CONTRACT.md:3-4 'rooted inside `obsidian.vault`'; ADAPTERS.md:136

criterion: caller whose contract changed not updated
finding: The Jira adapter manifest's configKeys still lists the removed jira.credentials-env and omits the new jira.site.
why: The schema change has a declared consumer that is now stale, and no later subtask's Scope covers this file.
fix: Replace jira.credentials-env with jira.site in configKeys.
evidence: adapter.json:25 `"jira.credentials-env"`; 0008 Scope lists adapters/tracker/jira/api.py and CONTRACT.md only

criterion: coverage ledger verdict not closed / closed-with-frontier
finding: The caller ledger for load() and the other changed symbols has no closure verdict, and its second test run section is empty.
why: Call sites are read off a ledger whose verdict is closed or closed-with-frontier; without one the caller set is not proven complete.
fix: Record the ledger's closure verdict with its frontier and fill in the second test run.
evidence: callers.md ends at `## Second test run` with no content; no line says closed or verdict

finding: validate FILE on the repository personal file, run from outside the checkout, treats it as the unfiltered env layer: no ignored-value warnings, and it accepts schema though load() refuses it.
why: With no git root, root becomes path.parent.parent, which is <repo>/.git for <repo>/.git/afk/config.yaml, so _validate_one finds no known layer.
fix: Work out the layer from the file's own location: a <git common dir>/afk/config.yaml path is the personal file.
evidence: probe: personal file `schema: 1`: load(r) raises `the shared overlay may not set schema`, while validate from outside gives problems [] and ignored []

finding: validate FILE layer detection has one test, for the committed file only.
why: _validate_one maps a path to five layers and refuses schema in two; only the repo branch is exercised.
fix: Parametrize the named-file validate test over the personal file, the local overlay and the machine file.
evidence: only named-file owner test: `file = committed(root, ...)` then `run(["validate", str(file)], root, home)`

finding: No test proves the commit-gate adoption check runs without Python, though the acceptance bullet requires it.
why: _commit_gates inherits a PATH that has Python, so a Python call in the check would go unnoticed.
fix: Run the gates with Python commands shadowed and assert the decision still comes out right.
evidence: Acceptance: "with no Python on the commit path; one test pins both answers"; environ = {**os.environ, ...} with no PATH override

finding: status reports a source file for a developer value the owner rule dropped.
why: source comes from raw read_block while value comes from the owner-filtered load(); for the machine-owned worktreeBasePath and worktreeRoot the personal file is named as source of a value nothing reads.
fix: Take source only from files whose layer the owner rule reads for that key.
evidence: developer_values.py:169 `source = next((label for label, p in files if p is not None and key in read_block(p)), None)`; probe: personal `worktreeBasePath: /custom/wt` gives `{need: required, value: null, source: repository}`

finding: Possible protocol inconsistency: validate writes the two kinds of warning line to different streams, and the (N warnings) count covers only path warnings.
why: Neither the count nor the stream tells a reader how many warnings there are.
fix: Send every warning to one stream and count or prefix the ignored-value lines.
evidence: afk-config.py:1431 `sys.stderr.write(f"afk-config: warning: {warning}\n")`; :1438 `sys.stdout.write("".join(f"afk-config: warning: {note}\n" for note in notes))`

criterion: caller whose contract changed not updated
finding: The plugin's own committed config now holds two values the owner rule ignores: notes (machine) and github.remote (personal).
why: validate warns on it and forge.sh stops passing --repo; no later Scope names the file.

finding: The jira.site check accepts strings that are not a site address, e.g. `https://a b`.
why: re.match with no end anchor checks only the start.
fix: Anchor the pattern, e.g. re.fullmatch(r"https?://[^/\s]+/?", site).

finding: Every CLI test's HOME points at one fixed directory in the system temp folder.
why: A file left there by any process changes every run() result: a hidden fixture shared across runs.
fix: Give run() an empty home of its own.

finding: Possibly easy to misuse: ignored_values returns bare tuples whose third field is an owner-rule sentence or the removed-key message.
why: A consumer must match prose to tell a removed key from a misplaced one.
fix: Return a named tuple with an owner-or-removed field.

finding: ignored_line is a new public name that neither SDD §8 nor Produces lists; only main calls it.
why: A public name in the shared reader is a contract importers may bind to.
